title: Where two seafloor models disagree
description: Absolute depth difference between two independent-ish global models, shown only where less than half of the 1′ cell is directly measured (TID 10–17) and the seafloor is deeper than 1,000 m (on shelves and slopes AUST is biased deep, so differences there are not shown). Large values mean the depth there is genuinely uncertain; small values do not prove it is right, because both models use satellite gravity.
mask: ocean (GEBCO TID != 0 and 1' elevation < 0), GEBCO depth >= 1000 m, measured fraction < 0.5, 75 S - 75 N, Caspian and Baikal excluded
citation: Yuan, J. & Yang, C. (2026) AUST_2026_BAT: A Global Bathymetry Model Derived from Multi-Scale Marine Gravity Anomalies Using Fully Connected Deep Neural Networks and Adaptive Multi-Factor Spatial Partitioning (v2026). Zenodo. doi:10.5281/zenodo.22711109
